answer_core:
Do not choose the advisor's hybrid direction yet. Treat two gates as controlling: Dr. Silva must be able to offer concrete data access, and the fallback plan must still be real enough to execute if the new direction fails.

In the next two weeks, run a short evidence check before committing. First, ask Dr. Silva what data exists, what access you would have, on what date, under whose approval, and what analysis would be feasible quickly enough to support a dissertation. Second, ask your advisor what support, time, resources, and authorship expectations would apply if you explore the hybrid direction, and what fully advisor-backed fallback remains available if it does not work.

Use Dr. Silva only as a low-cost reality check until your advisor has been consulted. Do not go around your advisor with a finished proposal. Do not run all three options in parallel. Do not let excitement about a hot field substitute for access, ownership, timeline, and a credible path to finish.

The key question is not whether option 3 sounds promising. It is whether it can become a dissertation without leaving you stranded. Commit only if Silva/data access is concrete and dated, the collaboration would be deep enough, your advisor supports the move, and the fallback is resourced, technically ready, identity-coherent, and protected by clear stop-loss criteria. Keep broad success-rate claims as humility checks, not as calibrated probabilities, unless you have evidence from a closely comparable dissertation setting.
